questions.text: Ritu completes 7/12 of a work in 21 days. In how many more days will she complete the remaining work at the same efficiency? रितु 21 दिनों में किसी िार्य िा 7/12 भाग पूिा ििती है। समान िक्षता से वह शेष िार्य कितने औि दिनों में पूिा ििेगी? (A) 15 days (B) 12 days (C) 18 days (D) 21 days (E) None of these
questions.prompt: Ritu completes 7/12 of a work in 21 days. In how many more days will she complete the remaining work at the same efficiency? रितु 21 दिनों में किसी िार्य िा 7/12 भाग पूिा ििती है। समान िक्षता से वह शेष िार्य कितने औि दिनों में पूिा ििेगी?
questions.explanation: 7/12 work is completed in 21 days. 1/12 work is completed in 21 ÷ 7 = 3 days. Remaining work = 1 − 7/12 = 5/12. Time for remaining work = 5 × 3 = 15 days. Final answer = 15 days.

questions.text: A clerk files 11 bundles of documents in 5 days. At the same rate, in how many days will he file 88 bundles? एि क्लि य 5 दिनों में िस्तावेजों िे 11 बंडल फाइल ििता है। समान िि से वह 88 बंडल कितने दिनों में फाइल ििेगा? (A) 35 days (B) 40 days (C) 36 days (D) 44 days (E) None of these
questions.prompt: A clerk files 11 bundles of documents in 5 days. At the same rate, in how many days will he file 88 bundles? एि क्लि य 5 दिनों में िस्तावेजों िे 11 बंडल फाइल ििता है। समान िि से वह 88 बंडल कितने दिनों में फाइल ििेगा?
questions.explanation: Time taken for 11 bundles = 5 days. Time taken for 88 bundles = 5 × 88 ÷ 11. Time taken = 5 × 8 = 40 days. Final answer = 40 days.

questions.text: Suresh completes 35% of a task in 7 days. In how many days will he complete the whole task? सुिेश 7 दिनों में किसी िार्य िा 35% पूिा ििता है। वह पूिा िार्य कितने दिनों में पूिा ििेगा? (A) 18 days (B) 24 days (C) 20 days (D) 28 days (E) None of these
questions.prompt: Suresh completes 35% of a task in 7 days. In how many days will he complete the whole task? सुिेश 7 दिनों में किसी िार्य िा 35% पूिा ििता है। वह पूिा िार्य कितने दिनों में पूिा ििेगा?
questions.explanation: 35% work is completed in 7 days. 100% work will be completed in 7 × 100 ÷ 35 days. Total time = 20 days. Final answer = 20 days.

questions.text: Arun can complete a job in 56 hours. How many hours does he need to complete 37.5% of the work? अरुण किसी िाम िो 56 घंटों में पूिा िि सिता है। िार्य िा 37.5% पूिा ििने िे ललए उसे कितने घंटे चादहए? (A) 28 hours (B) 18 hours (C) 24 hours (D) 21 hours (E) None of these
questions.prompt: Arun can complete a job in 56 hours. How many hours does he need to complete 37.5% of the work? अरुण किसी िाम िो 56 घंटों में पूिा िि सिता है। िार्य िा 37.5% पूिा ििने िे ललए उसे कितने घंटे चादहए?
questions.explanation: 37.5% = 3/8. Required time = 56 × 3/8. Required time = 21 hours. Final answer = 21 hours.

questions.text: Mahesh can complete a task in 80 days. If he works for 28 days, what percentage of the work is still incomplete? महेश किसी िार्य िो 80 दिनों में पूिा िि सिता है। र्दि वह 28 दिनों ति िाम ििता है, तो िार्य िा कितना प्रततशत अभी भी अधूिा है? (A) 55% (B) 60% (C) 70% (D) 65% (E) None of these
questions.prompt: Mahesh can complete a task in 80 days. If he works for 28 days, what percentage of the work is still incomplete? महेश किसी िार्य िो 80 दिनों में पूिा िि सिता है। र्दि वह 28 दिनों ति िाम ििता है, तो िार्य िा कितना प्रततशत अभी भी अधूिा है?
questions.explanation: Work completed in 28 days = 28/80 × 100. Work completed = 35%. Incomplete work = 100% − 35% = 65%. Final answer = 65%.

questions.text: Nikhil can complete a report in 14 days, while Kartik can complete the same report in 56 days. What is the ratio of Nikhil’s efficiency to Kartik’s efficiency? तनखिल एि रिपोटय 14 दिनों में पूिी िि सिता है, जबकि िाततयि वही रिपोटय 56 दिनों में पूिी िि सिता है। तनखिल िी िक्षता औि िाततयि िी िक्षता िा अनुपात क्र्ा है? (A) 1 : 4 (B) 2 : 3 (C) 4 : 1 (D) 3 : 4 (E) None of these
questions.prompt: Nikhil can complete a report in 14 days, while Kartik can complete the same report in 56 days. What is the ratio of Nikhil’s efficiency to Kartik’s efficiency? तनखिल एि रिपोटय 14 दिनों में पूिी िि सिता है, जबकि िाततयि वही रिपोटय 56 दिनों में पूिी िि सिता है। तनखिल िी िक्षता औि िाततयि िी िक्षता िा अनुपात क्र्ा है?
questions.explanation: Time ratio of Nikhil and Kartik = 14 : 56. Efficiency ratio is inverse of time ratio. Efficiency ratio of Nikhil and Kartik = 56 : 14 = 4 : 1. Final answer = 4 : 1.

questions.text: The time taken by P and Q to complete the same typing work is in the ratio 4 : 5. The efficiency of Q is what percent of the efficiency of P? P औि Q द्वािा समान टाइपपंग िार्य पूिा ििने में ललर्ा गर्ा समर् 4 : 5 िे अनुपात में है। Q िी िक्षता, P िी िक्षता िा कितना प्रततशत है? (A) 75% (B) 60% (C) 80% (D) 125% (E) None of these
questions.prompt: The time taken by P and Q to complete the same typing work is in the ratio 4 : 5. The efficiency of Q is what percent of the efficiency of P? P औि Q द्वािा समान टाइपपंग िार्य पूिा ििने में ललर्ा गर्ा समर् 4 : 5 िे अनुपात में है। Q िी िक्षता, P िी िक्षता िा कितना प्रततशत है?
questions.explanation: Time ratio of P and Q = 4 : 5. Efficiency ratio of P and Q = 5 : 4. Efficiency of Q as a percentage of P = 4/5 × 100. Efficiency of Q = 80%. Final answer = 80%.

questions.text: Diya completes a design work in 18 hours and Isha completes the same work in 27 hours. By what percent is Diya more efficient than Isha? दिर्ा एि डडजाइन िार्य 18 घंटों में पूिा ििती है औि ईशा वही िार्य 27 घंटों में पूिा ििती है। दिर्ा, ईशा से कितने प्रततशत अधधि िक्ष है? (A) 25% (B) 50% (C) 33 1/3% (D) 40% (E) None of these
questions.prompt: Diya completes a design work in 18 hours and Isha completes the same work in 27 hours. By what percent is Diya more efficient than Isha? दिर्ा एि डडजाइन िार्य 18 घंटों में पूिा ििती है औि ईशा वही िार्य 27 घंटों में पूिा ििती है। दिर्ा, ईशा से कितने प्रततशत अधधि िक्ष है?
questions.explanation: Efficiency ratio of Diya and Isha = 27 : 18. Efficiency ratio = 3 : 2. Diya is more efficient by 3 − 2 = 1 unit. Required percentage = 1/2 × 100 = 50%. Final answer = 50%.

questions.text: A completes 3/8 of a work in 12 days, while B completes 5/12 of the same work in 20 days. What is the ratio of A’s efficiency to B’s efficiency? A 12 दिनों में किसी िार्य िा 3/8 भाग पूिा ििता है, जबकि B उसी िार्य िा 5/12 भाग 20 दिनों में पूिा ििता है। A िी िक्षता औि B िी िक्षता िा अनुपात क्र्ा है? (A) 3 : 2 (B) 2 : 3 (C) 4 : 5 (D) 5 : 4 (E) None of these
questions.prompt: A completes 3/8 of a work in 12 days, while B completes 5/12 of the same work in 20 days. What is the ratio of A’s efficiency to B’s efficiency? A 12 दिनों में किसी िार्य िा 3/8 भाग पूिा ििता है, जबकि B उसी िार्य िा 5/12 भाग 20 दिनों में पूिा ििता है। A िी िक्षता औि B िी िक्षता िा अनुपात क्र्ा है?
questions.explanation: A’s 1 day work = 3/8 ÷ 12 = 3/(8 × 12) = 1/32. B’s 1 day work = 5/12 ÷ 20 = 5/(12 × 20) = 1/48. Efficiency ratio of A and B = 1/32 : 1/48. Required ratio = 48 : 32 = 3 : 2. Final answer = 3 : 2.

questions.text: Harsh is 25% more efficient than Manav. If Manav takes 7 days more than Harsh to complete a file-processing work, find the number of days taken by Harsh. हषय, मानव से 25% अधधि िक्ष है। र्दि मानव किसी फाइल-प्रोसेलसंग िार्य िो पूिा ििने में हषय से 7 दिन अधधि लेता है, तो हषय द्वािा ललए गए दिनों िी संख्र्ा ज्ञात िीजजए। (A) 35 days (B) 28 days (C) 21 days (D) 30 days (E) None of these
questions.prompt: Harsh is 25% more efficient than Manav. If Manav takes 7 days more than Harsh to complete a file-processing work, find the number of days taken by Harsh. हषय, मानव से 25% अधधि िक्ष है। र्दि मानव किसी फाइल-प्रोसेलसंग िार्य िो पूिा ििने में हषय से 7 दिन अधधि लेता है, तो हषय द्वािा ललए गए दिनों िी संख्र्ा ज्ञात िीजजए।
questions.explanation: Harsh is 25% more efficient than Manav. Efficiency ratio of Manav and Harsh = 4 : 5. Time ratio of Manav and Harsh = 5 : 4. Difference in time = 1 unit = 7 days. Time taken by Harsh = 4 × 7 = 28 days. Final answer = 28 days.

questions.text: Tanvi, Neha and Varun can complete a task in 20 days, 16 days and 10 days respectively. What is the respective ratio of their efficiencies? तन्वी, नेहा औि वरुण किसी िार्य िो क्रमशः 20 दिनों, 16 दिनों औि 10 दिनों में पूिा िि सिते हैं। उनिी िक्षताओं िा क्रमशः अनुपात क्र्ा है? (A) 4 : 5 : 8 (B) 5 : 4 : 8 (C) 8 : 5 : 4 (D) 4 : 8 : 5 (E) None of these
questions.prompt: Tanvi, Neha and Varun can complete a task in 20 days, 16 days and 10 days respectively. What is the respective ratio of their efficiencies? तन्वी, नेहा औि वरुण किसी िार्य िो क्रमशः 20 दिनों, 16 दिनों औि 10 दिनों में पूिा िि सिते हैं। उनिी िक्षताओं िा क्रमशः अनुपात क्र्ा है?
questions.explanation: Take total work = LCM of 20, 16 and 10 = 80 units. Tanvi’s efficiency = 80 ÷ 20 = 4 units/day. Neha’s efficiency = 80 ÷ 16 = 5 units/day. Varun’s efficiency = 80 ÷ 10 = 8 units/day. Required ratio = 4 : 5 : 8. Final answer = 4 : 5 : 8.

questions.text: A, B and C can complete a work in 35 days, 28 days and 70 days respectively. The efficiency of A is what percent of the efficiency of C? A, B औि C किसी िार्य िो क्रमशः 35 दिनों, 28 दिनों औि 70 दिनों में पूिा िि सिते हैं। A िी िक्षता, C िी िक्षता िा कितना प्रततशत है? (A) 150% (B) 200% (C) 250% (D) 300% (E) None of these
questions.prompt: A, B and C can complete a work in 35 days, 28 days and 70 days respectively. The efficiency of A is what percent of the efficiency of C? A, B औि C किसी िार्य िो क्रमशः 35 दिनों, 28 दिनों औि 70 दिनों में पूिा िि सिते हैं। A िी िक्षता, C िी िक्षता िा कितना प्रततशत है?

questions.text: Mohit, Rajesh and Kiran can do a piece of work in 36 days, 144 days and 24 days respectively. All start together, but Mohit and Kiran leave exactly 12 days before the work ends. How many days does it actually take to finish the work? मोहित, राजेश और किरण किसी िार्य िो क्रमशः 36 हिन, 144 हिन और 24 हिन में िर सिते िैं। सभी साथ में िार्य शुरू िरते िैं, लेकिन मोहित और किरण िार्य समाप्त िोने से ठीि 12 हिन पिले छोड़ िेते िैं। िार्य पूरा िोने में वास्तव में कितने हिन लगेंगे? (A) 18 days (B) 24 days (C) 20 days (D) 28 days (E) None of these
questions.prompt: Mohit, Rajesh and Kiran can do a piece of work in 36 days, 144 days and 24 days respectively. All start together, but Mohit and Kiran leave exactly 12 days before the work ends. How many days does it actually take to finish the work? मोहित, राजेश और किरण किसी िार्य िो क्रमशः 36 हिन, 144 हिन और 24 हिन में िर सिते िैं। सभी साथ में िार्य शुरू िरते िैं, लेकिन मोहित और किरण िार्य समाप्त िोने से ठीि 12 हिन पिले छोड़ िेते िैं। िार्य पूरा िोने में वास्तव में कितने हिन लगेंगे?
questions.explanation: Take total work = 144 units. Mohit’s efficiency = 144 ÷ 36 = 4 units/day. Rajesh’s efficiency = 144 ÷ 144 = 1 unit/day. Kiran’s efficiency = 144 ÷ 24 = 6 units/day. In the last 12 days, Rajesh alone works. Work done by Rajesh in last 12 days = 12 × 1 = 12 units. Remaining work before last 12 days = 144 − 12 = 132 units. Efficiency of all three together = 4 + 1 + 6 = 11 units/day. Time for first part = 132 ÷ 11 = 12 days. Total time = 12 + 12 = 24 days.

questions.text: Harsh, Aditya and Jatin can complete a piece of work in 30 days, 40 days and 120 days respectively. All start together; after 8 days Harsh leaves, then after 10 more days Aditya leaves. Jatin finishes the rest alone. How many total days are taken to finish the work? िर्य, आहित्र् और जततन किसी िार्य िो क्रमशः 30 हिन, 40 हिन और 120 हिन में पूरा िर सिते िैं। सभी साथ में िार्य शुरू िरते िैं; 8 हिन बाि िर्य छोड़ िेता िै, किर 10 और हिन बाि आहित्र् छोड़ िेता िै। शेर् िार्य जततन अि े ले पूरा िरता िै। िार्य पूरा िोने में िु ल कितने हिन लगेंगे? (A) 34 days (B) 30 days (C) 36 days (D) 40 days (E) None of these
questions.prompt: Harsh, Aditya and Jatin can complete a piece of work in 30 days, 40 days and 120 days respectively. All start together; after 8 days Harsh leaves, then after 10 more days Aditya leaves. Jatin finishes the rest alone. How many total days are taken to finish the work? िर्य, आहित्र् और जततन किसी िार्य िो क्रमशः 30 हिन, 40 हिन और 120 हिन में पूरा िर सिते िैं। सभी साथ में िार्य शुरू िरते िैं; 8 हिन बाि िर्य छोड़ िेता िै, किर 10 और हिन बाि आहित्र् छोड़ िेता िै। शेर् िार्य जततन अि े ले पूरा िरता िै। िार्य पूरा िोने में िु ल कितने हिन लगेंगे?
questions.explanation: Take total work = 120 units. Harsh’s efficiency = 120 ÷ 30 = 4 units/day. Aditya’s efficiency = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 units/day. Jatin’s efficiency = 120 ÷ 120 = 1 unit/day. Harsh works for 8 days. Work done by Harsh = 8 × 4 = 32 units. Aditya works for 18 days. Work done by Aditya = 18 × 3 = 54 units. Let total time = T days. Jatin works for T days. 32 + 54 + T = 120 T = 34 days.

questions.text: Anaya can finish a task in 36 days, Bhumi in 24 days and Chitra in 18 days. They begin together, but Anaya leaves 3 days before completion and Bhumi leaves 4 days before completion. In how many days is the task completed? अनर्ा किसी िार्य िो 36 हिन में, भूमम 24 हिन में और चित्रा 18 हिन में पूरा िर सिती िैं। वे साथ में िार्य शुरू िरती िैं, लेकिन अनर्ा िार्य पूरा िोने से 3 हिन पिले और भूमम 4 हिन पिले छोड़ िेती िै। िार्य कितने हिनों में पूरा िोगा? (A) 10 days (B) 12 days (C) 15 days (D) 8 days (E) None of these
questions.prompt: Anaya can finish a task in 36 days, Bhumi in 24 days and Chitra in 18 days. They begin together, but Anaya leaves 3 days before completion and Bhumi leaves 4 days before completion. In how many days is the task completed? अनर्ा किसी िार्य िो 36 हिन में, भूमम 24 हिन में और चित्रा 18 हिन में पूरा िर सिती िैं। वे साथ में िार्य शुरू िरती िैं, लेकिन अनर्ा िार्य पूरा िोने से 3 हिन पिले और भूमम 4 हिन पिले छोड़ िेती िै। िार्य कितने हिनों में पूरा िोगा?
questions.explanation: Take total work = 72 units. Anaya’s efficiency = 72 ÷ 36 = 2 units/day. Bhumi’s efficiency = 72 ÷ 24 = 3 units/day. Chitra’s efficiency = 72 ÷ 18 = 4 units/day. Let total time = T days. Anaya works for (T − 3) days. Bhumi works for (T − 4) days. Chitra works for T days. 2(T − 3) + 3(T − 4) + 4T = 72 2T − 6 + 3T − 12 + 4T = 72 9T − 18 = 72 9T = 90 T = 10 days.

questions.text: Naveen, Bhushan and Chirag are hired to complete a job. Naveen can finish it alone in 45 days, Bhushan in 30 days and Chirag in 18 days. All three begin together, but Naveen stops working 3 days after they start, and Bhushan stops working 4 days before the job is finished. In how many days is the job completed? नवीन, भूर्ण और चिराग िो एि िार्य पूरा िरने िे मलए रखा गर्ा िै। नवीन अि े ले इसे 45 हिन में, भूर्ण 30 हिन में और चिराग 18 हिन में पूरा िर सिता िै। तीनों साथ में िार्य शुरू िरते िैं, लेकिन नवीन शुरू िोने िे 3 हिन बाि िाम बंि िर िेता िै, और भूर्ण िार्य समाप्त िोने से 4 हिन पिले िाम बंि िर िेता िै। िार्य कितने हिनों में पूरा िोगा? (A) 15 days (B) 12 days (C) 18 days (D) 20 days (E) None of these
questions.prompt: Naveen, Bhushan and Chirag are hired to complete a job. Naveen can finish it alone in 45 days, Bhushan in 30 days and Chirag in 18 days. All three begin together, but Naveen stops working 3 days after they start, and Bhushan stops working 4 days before the job is finished. In how many days is the job completed? नवीन, भूर्ण और चिराग िो एि िार्य पूरा िरने िे मलए रखा गर्ा िै। नवीन अि े ले इसे 45 हिन में, भूर्ण 30 हिन में और चिराग 18 हिन में पूरा िर सिता िै। तीनों साथ में िार्य शुरू िरते िैं, लेकिन नवीन शुरू िोने िे 3 हिन बाि िाम बंि िर िेता िै, और भूर्ण िार्य समाप्त िोने से 4 हिन पिले िाम बंि िर िेता िै। िार्य कितने हिनों में पूरा िोगा?
questions.explanation: Take total work = 90 units. Naveen’s efficiency = 90 ÷ 45 = 2 units/day. Bhushan’s efficiency = 90 ÷ 30 = 3 units/day. Chirag’s efficiency = 90 ÷ 18 = 5 units/day. Naveen works for 3 days. Work done by Naveen = 3 × 2 = 6 units. Let total time = T days. Bhushan works for (T − 4) days. Chirag works for T days. 6 + 3(T − 4) + 5T = 90 6 + 3T − 12 + 5T = 90 8T − 6 = 90 8T = 96 T = 12 days.

questions.text: X can complete a task in 24 days and Y can complete it in 40 days. They start the task together, but Y leaves 8 days before completion. In how many days is the task completed? X किसी िार्य िो 24 हिन में और Y उसे 40 हिन में पूरा िर सिता िै। वे साथ में िार्य शुरू िरते िैं, लेकिन Y िार्य पूरा िोने से 8 हिन पिले छोड़ िेता िै। िार्य कितने हिनों में पूरा िोगा? (A) 18 days (B) 16 days (C) 20 days (D) 22 days (E) None of these
questions.prompt: X can complete a task in 24 days and Y can complete it in 40 days. They start the task together, but Y leaves 8 days before completion. In how many days is the task completed? X किसी िार्य िो 24 हिन में और Y उसे 40 हिन में पूरा िर सिता िै। वे साथ में िार्य शुरू िरते िैं, लेकिन Y िार्य पूरा िोने से 8 हिन पिले छोड़ िेता िै। िार्य कितने हिनों में पूरा िोगा?
questions.explanation: Take total work = 120 units. X’s efficiency = 120 ÷ 24 = 5 units/day. Y’s efficiency = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 units/day. Let total time = T days. Y works for (T − 8) days and X works for T days. 5T + 3(T − 8) = 120 5T + 3T − 24 = 120 8T = 144 T = 18 days.

questions.text: A can complete a work in 40 days and B can complete it in 24 days. They start together, but A leaves some days before completion. If the work is completed in 18 days, how many days before completion did A leave? A किसी िार्य िो 40 हिन में और B उसे 24 हिन में पूरा िर सिता िै। वे साथ में िार्य शुरू िरते िैं, लेकिन A िार्य पूरा िोने से िु छ हिन पिले छोड़ िेता िै। र्हि िार्य 18 हिन में पूरा िोता िै, तो A िार्य पूरा िोने से कितने हिन पिले छोड़ गर्ा? (A) 6 days (B) 8 days (C) 9 days (D) 7 days (E) None of these
questions.prompt: A can complete a work in 40 days and B can complete it in 24 days. They start together, but A leaves some days before completion. If the work is completed in 18 days, how many days before completion did A leave? A किसी िार्य िो 40 हिन में और B उसे 24 हिन में पूरा िर सिता िै। वे साथ में िार्य शुरू िरते िैं, लेकिन A िार्य पूरा िोने से िु छ हिन पिले छोड़ िेता िै। र्हि िार्य 18 हिन में पूरा िोता िै, तो A िार्य पूरा िोने से कितने हिन पिले छोड़ गर्ा?
questions.explanation: Take total work = 120 units. A’s efficiency = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 units/day. B’s efficiency = 120 ÷ 24 = 5 units/day. Let A leave x days before completion. A works for (18 − x) days and B works for 18 days. 3(18 − x) + 5 × 18 = 120 54 − 3x + 90 = 120 144 − 3x = 120 3x = 24 x = 8 days.

questions.text: A completes 1/3 of a work and then leaves. B finishes the remaining work in 28 days. If A and B together can complete the whole work in 21 days, in how many days can A alone complete the work? A किसी िार्य िा 1/3 भाग पूरा िरि े छोड़ िेता िै। B शेर् िार्य िो 28 हिन में पूरा िरता िै। र्हि A और B साथ में पूरा िार्य 21 हिन में िर सिते िैं, तो A अि े ले उस िार्य िो कितने हिनों में पूरा िरेगा? (A) 36 days (B) 54 days (C) 48 days (D) 42 days (E) None of these
questions.prompt: A completes 1/3 of a work and then leaves. B finishes the remaining work in 28 days. If A and B together can complete the whole work in 21 days, in how many days can A alone complete the work? A किसी िार्य िा 1/3 भाग पूरा िरि े छोड़ िेता िै। B शेर् िार्य िो 28 हिन में पूरा िरता िै। र्हि A और B साथ में पूरा िार्य 21 हिन में िर सिते िैं, तो A अि े ले उस िार्य िो कितने हिनों में पूरा िरेगा?
questions.explanation: B completes remaining work = 2/3 of total work. B completes 2/3 work in 28 days. So, B alone can complete whole work in 28 × 3 ÷ 2 = 42 days. A and B together can complete the work in 21 days. A’s 1 day work = 1/21 − 1/42 A’s 1 day work = 2/42 − 1/42 = 1/42 A alone can complete the work in 42 days.

questions.text: A, B and C can complete a work in 32 days, 48 days and 96 days respectively. All three start together. C leaves after 8 days, and B leaves 6 days before completion. In how many days is the work completed? A, B और C किसी िार्य िो क्रमशः 32 हिन, 48 हिन और 96 हिन में पूरा िर सिते िैं। तीनों साथ में िार्य शुरू िरते िैं। C 8 हिन बाि छोड़ िेता िै, और B िार्य पूरा िोने से 6 हिन पिले छोड़ िेता िै। िार्य कितने हिनों में पूरा िोगा? (A) 20 days (B) 22 days (C) 24 days (D) 18 days (E) None of these
questions.prompt: A, B and C can complete a work in 32 days, 48 days and 96 days respectively. All three start together. C leaves after 8 days, and B leaves 6 days before completion. In how many days is the work completed? A, B और C किसी िार्य िो क्रमशः 32 हिन, 48 हिन और 96 हिन में पूरा िर सिते िैं। तीनों साथ में िार्य शुरू िरते िैं। C 8 हिन बाि छोड़ िेता िै, और B िार्य पूरा िोने से 6 हिन पिले छोड़ िेता िै। िार्य कितने हिनों में पूरा िोगा?
questions.explanation: Take total work = 96 units. A’s efficiency = 96 ÷ 32 = 3 units/day. B’s efficiency = 96 ÷ 48 = 2 units/day. C’s efficiency = 96 ÷ 96 = 1 unit/day. Let total time = T days. A works for T days. B works for (T − 6) days. C works for 8 days. 3T + 2(T − 6) + 8 = 96 3T + 2T − 12 + 8 = 96 5T − 4 = 96 5T = 100 T = 20 days.

questions.text: M can complete a work in 9 days. M works for 5 days and the remaining work is completed by N in 16 days. In how many days can N alone complete the whole work? M किसी िार्य िो 9 हिन में पूरा िर सिता िै। M 5 हिन िार्य िरता िै और शेर् िार्य N द्वारा 16 हिन में पूरा किर्ा जाता िै। N अि े ले पूरा िार्य कितने हिनों में पूरा िरेगा? (A) 27 days (B) 36 days (C) 32 days (D) 30 days (E) None of these
questions.prompt: M can complete a work in 9 days. M works for 5 days and the remaining work is completed by N in 16 days. In how many days can N alone complete the whole work? M किसी िार्य िो 9 हिन में पूरा िर सिता िै। M 5 हिन िार्य िरता िै और शेर् िार्य N द्वारा 16 हिन में पूरा किर्ा जाता िै। N अि े ले पूरा िार्य कितने हिनों में पूरा िरेगा?
questions.explanation: M completes the work in 9 days. M works for 5 days, so remaining work = 4 days’ work of M. N completes 4 days’ work of M in 16 days. N will complete 9 days’ work of M in 16 × 9 ÷ 4 days. N alone time = 36 days.

questions.text: If Anu works on a task for 6 days, Bhavesh alone can complete the remaining work in 24 days. If Anu works on the task for 3 days, Bhavesh takes 30 days to complete the remaining work. In how many days can both together finish the task? र्हि अनु किसी िार्य पर 6 हिन िाम िरती िै, तो भावेश अि े ले शेर् िार्य 24 हिन में पूरा िर सिता िै। र्हि अनु 3 हिन िाम िरती िै, तो भावेश शेर् िार्य पूरा िरने में 30 हिन लेता िै। िोनों साथ में िार्य कितने हिनों में पूरा िरेंगे? (A) 10 days (B) 18 days (C) 15 days (D) 12 days (E) None of these
questions.prompt: If Anu works on a task for 6 days, Bhavesh alone can complete the remaining work in 24 days. If Anu works on the task for 3 days, Bhavesh takes 30 days to complete the remaining work. In how many days can both together finish the task? र्हि अनु किसी िार्य पर 6 हिन िाम िरती िै, तो भावेश अि े ले शेर् िार्य 24 हिन में पूरा िर सिता िै। र्हि अनु 3 हिन िाम िरती िै, तो भावेश शेर् िार्य पूरा िरने में 30 हिन लेता िै। िोनों साथ में िार्य कितने हिनों में पूरा िरेंगे?
questions.explanation: Let Anu’s efficiency = A and Bhavesh’s efficiency = B. Case 1: 6A + 24B = total work. Case 2: 3A + 30B = total work. Subtracting both equations: 3A = 6B A : B = 2 : 1 Let Anu’s efficiency = 2 units/day and Bhavesh’s efficiency = 1 unit/day. Total work = 6 × 2 + 24 × 1 = 36 units. Together efficiency = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day. Together time = 36 ÷ 3 = 12 days.

questions.text: If Charu works on a task for 6 days, the remaining task can be completed either by Dev alone in 24 days or by Charu and Dev together in 8 days. In how many days can Charu alone complete the whole task? र्हि िारू किसी िार्य पर 6 हिन िाम िरती िै, तो शेर् िार्य र्ा तो िेव अि े ले 24 हिन में पूरा िर सिता िै र्ा िारू और िेव साथ में 8 हिन में पूरा िर सिते िैं। िारू अि े ले पूरा िार्य कितने हिनों में पूरा िरेगी? (A) 16 days (B) 20 days (C) 18 days (D) 24 days (E) None of these
questions.prompt: If Charu works on a task for 6 days, the remaining task can be completed either by Dev alone in 24 days or by Charu and Dev together in 8 days. In how many days can Charu alone complete the whole task? र्हि िारू किसी िार्य पर 6 हिन िाम िरती िै, तो शेर् िार्य र्ा तो िेव अि े ले 24 हिन में पूरा िर सिता िै र्ा िारू और िेव साथ में 8 हिन में पूरा िर सिते िैं। िारू अि े ले पूरा िार्य कितने हिनों में पूरा िरेगी?
questions.explanation: Let the remaining work after Charu’s 6 days = R. Dev alone completes R in 24 days. Dev’s efficiency = R/24. Charu and Dev together complete R in 8 days. Together efficiency = R/8. Charu’s efficiency = R/8 − R/24 = 2R/24 = R/12. So, Charu alone completes remaining work R in 12 days. Charu has already worked 6 days. Total time for Charu alone to complete whole task = 6 + 12 = 18 days.

questions.text: If Ishaan works on a task with 50% efficiency for 20 days, Jatin can complete the remaining task in 45 days. If Ishaan works on the task with 75% efficiency for 20 days, Jatin can complete the remaining task in 30 days. If Ishaan completes 60% of the whole task at full efficiency, how many days will Jatin take to complete the remaining task? र्हि ईशान किसी िार्य पर 50% िक्षता से 20 हिन िाम िरता िै, तो जततन शेर् िार्य 45 हिन में पूरा िर सिता िै। र्हि ईशान 75% िक्षता से 20 हिन िाम िरता िै, तो जततन शेर् िार्य 30 हिन में पूरा िर सिता िै। र्हि ईशान पूरी िक्षता से पूरे िार्य िा 60% पूरा िरता िै, तो शेर् िार्य पूरा िरने में जततन िो कितने हिन लगेंगे? (A) 24 days (B) 27 days (C) 36 days (D) 30 days (E) None of these
questions.prompt: If Ishaan works on a task with 50% efficiency for 20 days, Jatin can complete the remaining task in 45 days. If Ishaan works on the task with 75% efficiency for 20 days, Jatin can complete the remaining task in 30 days. questions.explanation: Ishaan’s work in first case = 50% of 20 days = 10 full-efficiency days. Ishaan’s work in second case = 75% of 20 days = 15 full- efficiency days. Efficiency ratio of Ishaan and Jatin = 15 : 5 = 3 : 1. Let Ishaan’s efficiency = 3 units/day and Jatin’s efficiency = 1 unit/day. Total work = 10 × 3 + 45 × 1 = 75 units. Ishaan completes 60% of total work. Remaining work = 40% of 75 = 30 units. Jatin’s time = 30 ÷ 1 = 30 days.

questions.text: 12 men can finish a job in 16 days. 24 children can finish the same job in 24 days. If 1 man and 1 child work together, in how many days will they complete the job? 12 पुरुर् एि िार्य िो 16 हिन में पूरा िर सिते िैं। 24 बच्िे उसी िार्य िो 24 हिन में पूरा िर सिते िैं। र्हि 1 पुरुर् और 1 बच्िा साथ में िाम िरें, तो वे िार्य कितने हिनों में पूरा िरेंगे? (A) 144 days (B) 132 days (C) 120 days (D) 156 days (E) None of these Q1: Answer (B) Take total work = 144 units. Mohit’s efficiency = 144 ÷ 36 = 4 units/day. Rajesh’s efficiency = 144 ÷ 144 = 1 unit/day. Kiran’s efficiency = 144 ÷ 24 = 6 units/day. In the last 12 days, Rajesh alone works. Work done by Rajesh in last 12 days = 12 × 1 = 12 units. Remaining work before last 12 days = 144 − 12 = 132 units. Efficiency of all three together = 4 + 1 + 6 = 11 units/day. Time for first part = 132 ÷ 11 = 12 days. Total time = 12 + 12 = 24 days. Q2: Answer (A) Take total work = 120 units. Harsh’s efficiency = 120 ÷ 30 = 4 units/day. Aditya’s efficiency = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 units/day. Jatin’s efficiency = 120 ÷ 120 = 1 unit/day. Harsh works for 8 days. Work done by Harsh = 8 × 4 = 32 units. Aditya works for 18 days. Work done by Aditya = 18 × 3 = 54 units. Let total time = T days. Jatin works for T days. 32 + 54 + T = 120 T = 34 days. Q3: Answer (A) Take total work = 72 units. Anaya’s efficiency = 72 ÷ 36 = 2 units/day. Bhumi’s efficiency = 72 ÷ 24 = 3 units/day. Chitra’s efficiency = 72 ÷ 18 = 4 units/day. Let total time = T days. Anaya works for (T − 3) days. Bhumi works for (T − 4) days. Chitra works for T days. 2(T − 3) + 3(T − 4) + 4T = 72 2T − 6 + 3T − 12 + 4T = 72 9T − 18 = 72 9T = 90 T = 10 days. Q4: Answer (B) Take total work = 90 units. Naveen’s efficiency = 90 ÷ 45 = 2 units/day. Bhushan’s efficiency = 90 ÷ 30 = 3 units/day. Chirag’s efficiency = 90 ÷ 18 = 5 units/day. Naveen works for 3 days. Work done by Naveen = 3 × 2 = 6 units. Let total time = T days. Bhushan works for (T − 4) days. Chirag works for T days. 6 + 3(T − 4) + 5T = 90 6 + 3T − 12 + 5T = 90 8T − 6 = 90 8T = 96 T = 12 days. Q5: Answer (A) Take total work = 120 units. X’s efficiency = 120 ÷ 24 = 5 units/day. Y’s efficiency = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 units/day. Let total time = T days. Y works for (T − 8) days and X works for T days. 5T + 3(T − 8) = 120 5T + 3T − 24 = 120 8T = 144 T = 18 days. Q6: Answer (B) Take total work = 120 units. A’s efficiency = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 units/day. B’s efficiency = 120 ÷ 24 = 5 units/day. Let A leave x days before completion. A works for (18 − x) days and B works for 18 days. 3(18 − x) + 5 × 18 = 120 54 − 3x + 90 = 120 144 − 3x = 120 3x = 24 x = 8 days. Q7: Answer (D) B completes remaining work = 2/3 of total work. B completes 2/3 work in 28 days. So, B alone can complete whole work in 28 × 3 ÷ 2 = 42 days. A and B together can complete the work in 21 days. A’s 1 day work = 1/21 − 1/42 A’s 1 day work = 2/42 − 1/42 = 1/42 A alone can complete the work in 42 days. Q8: Answer (A) Take total work = 96 units. A’s efficiency = 96 ÷ 32 = 3 units/day. B’s efficiency = 96 ÷ 48 = 2 units/day. C’s efficiency = 96 ÷ 96 = 1 unit/day. Let total time = T days. A works for T days. B works for (T − 6) days. C works for 8 days. 3T + 2(T − 6) + 8 = 96 3T + 2T − 12 + 8 = 96 5T − 4 = 96 5T = 100 T = 20 days. Q9: Answer (B) M completes the work in 9 days. M works for 5 days, so remaining work = 4 days’ work of M. N completes 4 days’ work of M in 16 days. N will complete 9 days’ work of M in 16 × 9 ÷ 4 days. N alone time = 36 days. Q10: Answer (D) Let Anu’s efficiency = A and Bhavesh’s efficiency = B. Case 1: 6A + 24B = total work. Case 2: 3A + 30B = total work. Subtracting both equations: 3A = 6B A : B = 2 : 1 Let Anu’s efficiency = 2 units/day and Bhavesh’s efficiency = 1 unit/day. Total work = 6 × 2 + 24 × 1 = 36 units. Together efficiency = 2 + 1 = 3 units/day. Together time = 36 ÷ 3 = 12 days. Q11: Answer (C) Let the remaining work after Charu’s 6 days = R. Dev alone completes R in 24 days. Dev’s efficiency = R/24. Charu and Dev together complete R in 8 days. Together efficiency = R/8. Charu’s efficiency = R/8 − R/24 = 2R/24 = R/12. So, Charu alone completes remaining work R in 12 days. Charu has already worked 6 days. Total time for Charu alone to complete whole task = 6 + 12 = 18 days. Q12: Answer (D) Ishaan’s work in first case = 50% of 20 days = 10 full-efficiency days. Ishaan’s work in second case = 75% of 20 days = 15 full- efficiency days. Difference = 5 full-efficiency days of Ishaan. Jatin’s time difference = 45 − 30 = 15 days. So, 5 days of Ishaan’s work = 15 days of Jatin’s work. Efficiency ratio of Ishaan and Jatin = 15 : 5 = 3 : 1. Let Ishaan’s efficiency = 3 units/day and Jatin’s efficiency = 1 unit/day. Total work = 10 × 3 + 45 × 1 = 75 units. Ishaan completes 60% of total work. Remaining work = 40% of 75 = 30 units. Jatin’s time = 30 ÷ 1 = 30 days. Q13: Answer (C) Take total work = 30 units. Aditya’s efficiency = 30 ÷ 15 = 2 units/day. Kartik’s efficiency = 30 ÷ 30 = 1 unit/day. They work alternately, starting with Aditya. Work done in 2 days = 2 + 1 = 3 units. Number of 2-day cycles = 30 ÷ 3 = 10 cycles. Total time = 10 × 2 = 20 days. Q14: Answer (A) Take total work = 75 units. A’s efficiency = 75 ÷ 15 = 5 units/day. B’s efficiency = 75 ÷ 25 = 3 units/day. They start with B. Work done in 2 days = 3 + 5 = 8 units. Work done in 18 days = 9 × 8 = 72 units. Remaining work = 75 − 72 = 3 units. On the 19th day, B completes 3 units. Total time = 19 days. Q15: Answer (A) Take total work = 84 units. Manav’s efficiency = 84 ÷ 21 = 4 units/day. Sahil’s efficiency = 84 ÷ 28 = 3 units/day. They start with Manav. Work done in 2 days = 4 + 3 = 7 units. Number of 2-day cycles = 84 ÷ 7 = 12 cycles. Total time = 12 × 2 = 24 days. Q16: Answer (D) In 19 days, Ishaan works for 10 days and Gaurav works for 9 days. Ishaan’s 1 day work = 1/(K + 7). Gaurav’s 1 day work = 1/(K + 19). 10/(K + 7) + 9/(K + 19) = 1 10(K + 19) + 9(K + 7) = (K + 7)(K + 19) 10K + 190 + 9K + 63 = K² + 26K + 133 19K + 253 = K² + 26K + 133 K² + 7K − 120 = 0 (K + 15)(K − 8) = 0 K = 8. Q17: Answer (D) Let Deepak’s efficiency = 2 units/day. Amit is 50% more efficient than Deepak. Amit’s efficiency = 3 units/day. Normal work = 20 × 2 = 40 units. New work is 50% more than normal work. New work = 40 × 150/100 = 60 units. They work alternately, starting with Amit. Work done in 2 days = 3 + 2 = 5 units. Number of 2-day cycles = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 cycles. Total time = 12 × 2 = 24 days. Q18: Answer (A) Take total work = 144 units. Ravi’s efficiency = 144 ÷ 36 = 4 units/day. Suman’s efficiency = 144 ÷ 72 = 2 units/day. Ketan’s efficiency = 144 ÷ 48 = 3 units/day. Work done in 3 days = 4 + 2 + 3 = 9 units. Work done in 45 days = 15 × 9 = 135 units. Remaining work = 144 − 135 = 9 units. Next Ravi does 4 units, remaining = 5 units. Next Suman does 2 units, remaining = 3 units. Next Ketan does 3 units and completes the work. Additional days = 3 days. Total time = 45 + 3 = 48 days. Q19: Answer (A) Take total work = 126 units. A’s efficiency = 126 ÷ 42 = 3 units/day. B’s efficiency = 126 ÷ 63 = 2 units/day. C’s efficiency = 126 ÷ 126 = 1 unit/day. Order is B, C and A. Work done in 3 days = 2 + 1 + 3 = 6 units. Number of 3-day cycles = 126 ÷ 6 = 21 cycles. Total time = 21 × 3 = 63 days. Q20: Answer (D) Take total work = 80 units. Ramesh’s efficiency = 80 ÷ 16 = 5 units/day. Uday’s efficiency = 80 ÷ 40 = 2 units/day. They start with Ramesh. In 10 days, they complete 5 cycles. Work done in 10 days = 5 × (5 + 2) = 35 units. On the 11th day, Ramesh works. Work done on 11th day = 5 units. Total work done in 11 days = 35 + 5 = 40 units. Remaining work = 80 − 40 = 40 units. Additional time required by Ramesh = 40 ÷ 5 = 8 days. Q21: Answer (A) Efficiency ratio of Kapil and Mohan = 3 : 4. They work alternately, starting with Kapil. In 11 days, Kapil works for 6 days and Mohan works for 5 days. Work done by Kapil = 6 × 3 = 18 units. Work done by Mohan = 5 × 4 = 20 units. Payment ratio of Kapil and Mohan = 18 : 20 = 9 : 10. Mohan’s share = 28500 × 10 ÷ 19 Mohan’s share = Rs. 15000. Q22: Answer (D) Efficiency ratio of A and B = 7 : 5. They work alternately, starting with B. In 13 days, B works for 7 days and A works for 6 days. Work done by A = 6 × 7 = 42 units. Work done by B = 7 × 5 = 35 units. Payment ratio of A and B = 42 : 35 = 6 : 5. A’s share = 55000 × 6 ÷ 11 A’s share = Rs. 30000. Q23: Answer (D) Take total work = 180 units. Combined efficiency of Aditya, Varun and Nitin = 180 ÷ 15 = 12 units/day. Varun’s efficiency = 180 ÷ 30 = 6 units/day. Nitin’s efficiency = 180 ÷ 90 = 2 units/day. Aditya’s efficiency = 12 − 6 − 2 = 4 units/day. Day 1 work = Aditya + Varun = 4 + 6 = 10 units. Day 2 work = Nitin + Varun = 2 + 6 = 8 units. Work done in 2 days = 18 units. Total work = 180 units, so 10 cycles are required. Nitin works once in each cycle, so Nitin works for 10 days. Nitin’s work = 10 × 2 = 20 units. Nitin’s share = 18000 × 20 ÷ 180 Nitin’s share = Rs. 2000. Q24: Answer (A) Let the initial number of workers = p. Initial time = 84 days. With 28 fewer workers, time = 84 + 21 = 105 days. Total work remains same. p × 84 = (p − 28) × 105 84p = 105p − 2940 21p = 2940 p = 140 workers. Q25: Answer (A) 42 workers can finish the task in 54 days. They work for 18 days. Remaining planned work = 54 − 18 = 36 days’ work of 42 workers. After 14 workers leave, remaining workers = 42 − 14 = 28. 28 workers are 2/3 of 42 workers. So time required becomes 3/2 times. Time required after workers leave = 36 × 3 ÷ 2 = 54 days. Total time = 18 + 54 = 72 days. Q26: Answer (D) 64 workers can complete the project in 45 days. They work for 15 days. Remaining planned time = 45 − 15 = 30 days. Project is completed 10 days before planned time. Actual remaining time = 30 − 10 = 20 days. Workers required become 30 ÷ 20 = 3/2 times. Total workers required = 64 × 3 ÷ 2 = 96 workers. Extra workers = 96 − 64 = 32 workers. Q27: Answer (B) After 9 workers leave, remaining workers = 36 − 9 = 27. 27 is 3/4 of 36. So, time for remaining work becomes 4/3 times. Increase in total time = 75 − 60 = 15 days. This increase is 1/3 of the planned remaining time. Planned remaining time = 15 × 3 = 45 days. Therefore, v = 60 − 45 = 15 days. Q28: Answer (B) Take total work = 50 × 48 = 2400 worker-units. Work done in first 16 days = 50 × 16 = 800 worker-units. Remaining work = 2400 − 800 = 1600 worker-units. After 16 days, 10 workers leave, so old workers left = 40. 20 new workers join, each twice as efficient as an old worker. Equivalent workers = 40 + 20 × 2 = 80. Time after replacement = 1600 ÷ 80 = 20 days. Total time = 16 + 20 = 36 days. Q29: Answer (C) Remaining planned time after 12 days = 48 − 12 = 36 days. Work is completed 12 days before scheduled time. Actual remaining time = 36 − 12 = 24 days. Required equivalent workers = 48 × 36 ÷ 24 = 72. Extra equivalent workers required = 72 − 48 = 24. Each new worker is 50% more efficient than an old worker. Efficiency of each new worker = 3/2 old worker. Number of new workers = 24 ÷ 3/2 = 16 workers. Q30: Answer (A) Remaining planned work after 14 days = 35 − 14 = 21 days’ work of 72 workers. After 18 workers leave, workers left = 72 − 18 = 54. Time required for remaining work = 72 × 21 ÷ 54 = 28 days. Total time = 14 + 28 = 42 days. Delay = 42 − 35 = 7 days. Q31: Answer (C) 24 men can build the wall in 18 days. They work for 8 days. Accident destroys 50% of completed work. Destroyed work = 50% of 8 days’ work = 4 days’ work. Extra time needed = 4 days. Total time = 18 + 4 = 22 days. Q32: Answer (D) Remaining time after 48 days = 72 − 48 = 24 days. After hiring 80 additional workers, total workers = 160 + 80 = 240. Remaining work is completed by 240 workers in 24 days. Without additional workers, 160 workers would take: 24 × 240 ÷ 160 = 36 days. Delay = 36 − 24 = 12 days. Q33: Answer (C) One-third work is done by 80 men in 24 days. Total work = 80 × 24 × 3 = 5760 labourer-days. Remaining work = 2/3 × 5760 = 3840 labourer-days. Scheduled time = 60 days. Required completion time = 60 − 6 = 54 days. Remaining time = 54 − 24 = 30 days. Required men = 3840 ÷ 30 = 128. More men required = 128 − 80 = 48 men. Q34: Answer (D) 40 men can build the wall in 40 days. They work for 9 days. Storm destroys 4/9 of the work done. Destroyed work = 4/9 of 9 days’ work = 4 days’ work. Effective completed work = 9 − 4 = 5 days’ work. Remaining work = 40 − 5 = 35 days’ work of 40 men. Number of workers decreases by 30%, so remaining workers = 70% of original. Time required = 35 × 100 ÷ 70 Time required = 50 days. Q35: Answer (B) Planned time = 42 days. Actual total time = 53 days. Extra time over planned time = 53 − 42 = 11 days. They work for 12 days before rain. Damaged work = 25% of 12 days’ work = 3 days’ work. Extra time = stoppage time + time to redo damaged work. x + 3 = 11 x = 8. Q36: Answer (C) Let the initial number of workers = W. 37.5% = 3/8. 45W worker-days complete 3/8 of the work. Total work = 45W ÷ 3/8 = 120W. Remaining work = 5/8 × 120W = 75W. Remaining time = 100 − 45 = 55 days. Workers after adding 32 more = W + 32. (W + 32) × 55 = 75W 55W + 1760 = 75W 20W = 1760 W = 88 workers. Q37: Answer (A) 25% work is completed by 30 men in 20 days. Work done = 30 × 20 = 600 man-days. Total work = 600 × 4 = 2400 man-days. Remaining work = 75% of 2400 = 1800 man-days. Remaining time = 60 − 20 = 40 days. Required men = 1800 ÷ 40 = 45. More men required = 45 − 30 = 15 men. Q38: Answer (A) Work done by 40 workers in 10 days at 7 hours/day = 40 × 7 × 10 = 2800 worker-hours. This is 5/14 of total work. Total work = 2800 × 14 ÷ 5 = 7840 worker-hours. Remaining work = 9/14 × 7840 = 5040 worker-hours. Each worker now works 8 hours daily for 15 days. Work by one worker = 15 × 8 = 120 worker-hours. Required workers = 5040 ÷ 120 = 42 workers. Q39: Answer (B) Initial food = 1080 soldiers for 50 days. Food consumed in 32 days = 1080 × 32 soldier-days. Remaining food = 1080 × (50 − 32) = 1080 × 18 soldier-days. Soldiers left = 1080 − 360 = 720. More days = 1080 × 18 ÷ 720 More days = 27 days. Q40: Answer (C) Remaining grain after 36 days = 1600 × (60 − 36) × 500 g. Remaining grain = 1600 × 24 × 500 g. Remaining people = 1600 − 400 = 1200. Each remaining person consumes 640 g daily. Let leftover grain last for x days. 1200 × x × 640 = 1600 × 24 × 500 x = (1600 × 24 × 500) ÷ (1200 × 640) x = 25 days. Q41: Answer (A) 3/4 work is completed by 120 workers in 72 days at 9 hours/day. Work for 3/4 part = 120 × 72 × 9 worker-hours. Work for 1/4 part = 120 × 72 × 9 ÷ 3 = 25920 worker-hours. Remaining time = 90 − 72 = 18 days. Each worker now works 10 hours daily. Required workers = 25920 ÷ (18 × 10) = 144. Additional workers = 144 − 120 = 24 workers. Q42: Answer (D) Let the efficiency of each worker = 1 unit/day. Rohit alone takes 276 days, so total work = 276 units. Workers per day are 1, 2, 3, ..., n. Work done in n days = 1 + 2 + 3 + ... + n n(n + 1)/2 = 276 23 × 24 ÷ 2 = 276 n = 23 days. Q43: Answer (D) Let initial number of workers = x. If no worker left, work would be completed in 12 days. Total work = 12x worker-days. Workers over 18 days form an AP: x, x − 6, x − 12, ..., x − 102. Total work done in 18 days = 18/2 × [2x − 17 × 6] = 9(2x − 102) So, 12x = 9(2x − 102) 12x = 18x − 918 6x = 918 x = 153 workers. Q44: Answer (B) Let the efficiency of one worker = 1 unit/day. One worker completes the work in 396 days, so total work = 396 units. Workers over n days are 5, 7, 9, ... This is an AP with first term 5 and common difference 2. Work done in n days = n/2 × [2 × 5 + (n − 1) × 2] = n/2 × [10 + 2n − 2] = n/2 × (2n + 8) = n(n + 4) n(n + 4) = 396 18 × 22 = 396 n = 18 days. Q45: Answer (E) Take total work = 72 units. A’s efficiency = 72 ÷ 24 = 3 units/day. B’s efficiency = 72 ÷ 36 = 2 units/day. C’s spoiling efficiency = 72 ÷ 72 = 1 unit/day. A and B together complete 3 + 2 = 5 units/day. Net work in one full 3-day cycle = 5 + 5 − 1 = 9 units. After 7 full cycles = 7 × 9 = 63 units completed. Remaining work = 72 − 63 = 9 units. Day 22: A and B complete 5 units. Remaining work = 9 − 5 = 4 units. Day 23: A and B can complete 5 units in 1 day. Time to complete remaining 4 units = 4/5 day. Total time = 21 + 1 + 4/5 = 22.8 days. 22.8 days is not given in options A–D. Therefore, answer is None of these. Q46: Answer (D) Given time is same for 18 men and 24 women. So, work done by 18 men = work done by 24 women. 18 men = 24 women. Efficiency ratio of one man to one woman = 24 : 18 = 4 : 3. A woman is less efficient by 4 − 3 = 1 unit on a base of 4 units. Required percentage = 1/4 × 100 = 25%. Q47: Answer (B) For the same work: 16 men × 18 days = 24 women × 16 days 288M = 384W M : W = 384 : 288 M : W = 4 : 3. Q48: Answer (A) Take total work = 72 units. Efficiency of one man = 72 ÷ 36 = 2 units/day. Efficiency of one woman = 72 ÷ 72 = 1 unit/day. Efficiency of 3 men and 6 women = 3 × 2 + 6 × 1 = 6 + 6 = 12 units/day. Time taken = 72 ÷ 12 = 6 days. Q49: Answer (C) Take total work = 80 units. Efficiency of one man = 80 ÷ 40 = 2 units/day. Efficiency of one woman = 80 ÷ 80 = 1 unit/day. Total efficiency of 6 men and 4 women = 6 × 2 + 4 × 1 = 12 + 4 = 16 units/day. Time taken = 80 ÷ 16 = 5 days. Q50: Answer (A) 12 men can finish the job in 16 days. So, one man alone can complete the job in 12 × 16 = 192 days. 24 children can finish the job in 24 days. So, one child alone can complete the job in 24 × 24 = 576 days. Together time for 1 man and 1 child: = 192 × 576 ÷ (192 + 576) = 110592 ÷ 768 = 144 days.

Gaurav’s 1 day work = 1/(K + 19). 10/(K + 7) + 9/(K + 19) = 1 10(K + 19) + 9(K + 7) = (K + 7)(K + 19) 10K + 190 + 9K + 63 = K² + 26K + 133 19K + 253 = K² + 26K + 133 K² + 7K − 120 = 0 (K + 15)(K − 8) = 0 K = 8. Q17: Answer

Let Deepak’s efficiency = 2 units/day. Amit is 50% more efficient than Deepak. Amit’s efficiency = 3 units/day. Normal work = 20 × 2 = 40 units. New work is 50% more than normal work. New work = 40 × 150/100 = 60 units. They work alternately, starting with Amit. Work done in 2 days = 3 + 2 = 5 units. Number of 2-day cycles = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 cycles. Total time = 12 × 2 = 24 days. Q18: Answer

Take total work = 144 units. Ravi’s efficiency = 144 ÷ 36 = 4 units/day. Suman’s efficiency = 144 ÷ 72 = 2 units/day. Ketan’s efficiency = 144 ÷ 48 = 3 units/day. Work done in 3 days = 4 + 2 + 3 = 9 units. Work done in 45 days = 15 × 9 = 135 units. Remaining work = 144 − 135 = 9 units. Next Ravi does 4 units, remaining = 5 units. Next Suman does 2 units, remaining = 3 units. Next Ketan does 3 units and completes the work. Additional days = 3 days. Total time = 45 + 3 = 48 days. Q19: Answer

Take total work = 126 units. A’s efficiency = 126 ÷ 42 = 3 units/day. B’s efficiency = 126 ÷ 63 = 2 units/day. C’s efficiency = 126 ÷ 126 = 1 unit/day. Order is B, C and A. Work done in 3 days = 2 + 1 + 3 = 6 units. Number of 3-day cycles = 126 ÷ 6 = 21 cycles. Total time = 21 × 3 = 63 days. Q20: Answer

Take total work = 80 units. Ramesh’s efficiency = 80 ÷ 16 = 5 units/day. Uday’s efficiency = 80 ÷ 40 = 2 units/day. They start with Ramesh. In 10 days, they complete 5 cycles. Work done in 10 days = 5 × (5 + 2) = 35 units. On the 11th day, Ramesh works. Work done on 11th day = 5 units. Total work done in 11 days = 35 + 5 = 40 units. Remaining work = 80 − 40 = 40 units. Additional time required by Ramesh = 40 ÷ 5 = 8 days. Q21: Answer

Efficiency ratio of Kapil and Mohan = 3 : 4. They work alternately, starting with Kapil. In 11 days, Kapil works for 6 days and Mohan works for 5 days. Work done by Kapil = 6 × 3 = 18 units. Work done by Mohan = 5 × 4 = 20 units. Payment ratio of Kapil and Mohan = 18 : 20 = 9 : 10. Mohan’s share = 28500 × 10 ÷ 19 Mohan’s share = Rs. 15000. Q22: Answer

Efficiency ratio of A and B = 7 : 5. They work alternately, starting with B. In 13 days, B works for 7 days and A works for 6 days. Work done by A = 6 × 7 = 42 units. Work done by B = 7 × 5 = 35 units. Payment ratio of A and B = 42 : 35 = 6 : 5. A’s share = 55000 × 6 ÷ 11 A’s share = Rs. 30000. Q23: Answer

Take total work = 180 units. Combined efficiency of Aditya, Varun and Nitin = 180 ÷ 15 = 12 units/day. Varun’s efficiency = 180 ÷ 30 = 6 units/day. Nitin’s efficiency = 180 ÷ 90 = 2 units/day. Aditya’s efficiency = 12 − 6 − 2 = 4 units/day. Day 1 work = Aditya + Varun = 4 + 6 = 10 units. Day 2 work = Nitin + Varun = 2 + 6 = 8 units. Work done in 2 days = 18 units. Total work = 180 units, so 10 cycles are required. Nitin works once in each cycle, so Nitin works for 10 days. Nitin’s work = 10 × 2 = 20 units. Nitin’s share = 18000 × 20 ÷ 180 Nitin’s share = Rs. 2000. Q24: Answer

Let the initial number of workers = p. Initial time = 84 days. With 28 fewer workers, time = 84 + 21 = 105 days. Total work remains same. p × 84 = (p − 28) × 105 84p = 105p − 2940 21p = 2940 p = 140 workers. Q25: Answer

42 workers can finish the task in 54 days. They work for 18 days. Remaining planned work = 54 − 18 = 36 days’ work of 42 workers. After 14 workers leave, remaining workers = 42 − 14 = 28. 28 workers are 2/3 of 42 workers. So time required becomes 3/2 times. Time required after workers leave = 36 × 3 ÷ 2 = 54 days. Total time = 18 + 54 = 72 days. Q26: Answer

64 workers can complete the project in 45 days. They work for 15 days. Remaining planned time = 45 − 15 = 30 days. Project is completed 10 days before planned time. Actual remaining time = 30 − 10 = 20 days. Workers required become 30 ÷ 20 = 3/2 times. Total workers required = 64 × 3 ÷ 2 = 96 workers. Extra workers = 96 − 64 = 32 workers. Q27: Answer

After 9 workers leave, remaining workers = 36 − 9 = 27. 27 is 3/4 of 36. So, time for remaining work becomes 4/3 times. Increase in total time = 75 − 60 = 15 days. This increase is 1/3 of the planned remaining time. Planned remaining time = 15 × 3 = 45 days. Therefore, v = 60 − 45 = 15 days. Q28: Answer

Take total work = 50 × 48 = 2400 worker-units. Work done in first 16 days = 50 × 16 = 800 worker-units. Remaining work = 2400 − 800 = 1600 worker-units. After 16 days, 10 workers leave, so old workers left = 40. 20 new workers join, each twice as efficient as an old worker. Equivalent workers = 40 + 20 × 2 = 80. Time after replacement = 1600 ÷ 80 = 20 days. Total time = 16 + 20 = 36 days. Q29: Answer

Remaining planned time after 12 days = 48 − 12 = 36 days. Work is completed 12 days before scheduled time. Actual remaining time = 36 − 12 = 24 days. Required equivalent workers = 48 × 36 ÷ 24 = 72. Extra equivalent workers required = 72 − 48 = 24. Each new worker is 50% more efficient than an old worker. Efficiency of each new worker = 3/2 old worker. Number of new workers = 24 ÷ 3/2 = 16 workers. Q30: Answer

Remaining planned work after 14 days = 35 − 14 = 21 days’ work of 72 workers. After 18 workers leave, workers left = 72 − 18 = 54. Time required for remaining work = 72 × 21 ÷ 54 = 28 days. Total time = 14 + 28 = 42 days. Delay = 42 − 35 = 7 days. Q31: Answer

24 men can build the wall in 18 days. They work for 8 days. Accident destroys 50% of completed work. Destroyed work = 50% of 8 days’ work = 4 days’ work. Extra time needed = 4 days. Total time = 18 + 4 = 22 days. Q32: Answer

Remaining time after 48 days = 72 − 48 = 24 days. After hiring 80 additional workers, total workers = 160 + 80 = 240. Remaining work is completed by 240 workers in 24 days. Without additional workers, 160 workers would take: 24 × 240 ÷ 160 = 36 days. Delay = 36 − 24 = 12 days. Q33: Answer

One-third work is done by 80 men in 24 days. Total work = 80 × 24 × 3 = 5760 labourer-days. Remaining work = 2/3 × 5760 = 3840 labourer-days. Scheduled time = 60 days. Required completion time = 60 − 6 = 54 days. Remaining time = 54 − 24 = 30 days. Required men = 3840 ÷ 30 = 128. More men required = 128 − 80 = 48 men. Q34: Answer

40 men can build the wall in 40 days. They work for 9 days. Storm destroys 4/9 of the work done. Destroyed work = 4/9 of 9 days’ work = 4 days’ work. Effective completed work = 9 − 4 = 5 days’ work. Remaining work = 40 − 5 = 35 days’ work of 40 men. Number of workers decreases by 30%, so remaining workers = 70% of original. Time required = 35 × 100 ÷ 70 Time required = 50 days. Q35: Answer

Planned time = 42 days. Actual total time = 53 days. Extra time over planned time = 53 − 42 = 11 days. They work for 12 days before rain. Damaged work = 25% of 12 days’ work = 3 days’ work. Extra time = stoppage time + time to redo damaged work. x + 3 = 11 x = 8. Q36: Answer

Let the initial number of workers = W. 37.5% = 3/8. 45W worker-days complete 3/8 of the work. Total work = 45W ÷ 3/8 = 120W. Remaining work = 5/8 × 120W = 75W. Remaining time = 100 − 45 = 55 days. Workers after adding 32 more = W + 32. (W + 32) × 55 = 75W 55W + 1760 = 75W 20W = 1760 W = 88 workers. Q37: Answer

25% work is completed by 30 men in 20 days. Work done = 30 × 20 = 600 man-days. Total work = 600 × 4 = 2400 man-days. Remaining work = 75% of 2400 = 1800 man-days. Remaining time = 60 − 20 = 40 days. Required men = 1800 ÷ 40 = 45. More men required = 45 − 30 = 15 men. Q38: Answer

Work done by 40 workers in 10 days at 7 hours/day = 40 × 7 × 10 = 2800 worker-hours. This is 5/14 of total work. Total work = 2800 × 14 ÷ 5 = 7840 worker-hours. Remaining work = 9/14 × 7840 = 5040 worker-hours. Each worker now works 8 hours daily for 15 days. Work by one worker = 15 × 8 = 120 worker-hours. Required workers = 5040 ÷ 120 = 42 workers. Q39: Answer

Initial food = 1080 soldiers for 50 days. Food consumed in 32 days = 1080 × 32 soldier-days. Remaining food = 1080 × (50 − 32) = 1080 × 18 soldier-days. Soldiers left = 1080 − 360 = 720. More days = 1080 × 18 ÷ 720 More days = 27 days. Q40: Answer

Remaining grain after 36 days = 1600 × (60 − 36) × 500 g. Remaining grain = 1600 × 24 × 500 g. Remaining people = 1600 − 400 = 1200. Each remaining person consumes 640 g daily. Let leftover grain last for x days. 1200 × x × 640 = 1600 × 24 × 500 x = (1600 × 24 × 500) ÷ (1200 × 640) x = 25 days. Q41: Answer

3/4 work is completed by 120 workers in 72 days at 9 hours/day. Work for 3/4 part = 120 × 72 × 9 worker-hours. Work for 1/4 part = 120 × 72 × 9 ÷ 3 = 25920 worker-hours. Remaining time = 90 − 72 = 18 days. Each worker now works 10 hours daily. Required workers = 25920 ÷ (18 × 10) = 144. Additional workers = 144 − 120 = 24 workers. Q42: Answer

Let the efficiency of each worker = 1 unit/day. Rohit alone takes 276 days, so total work = 276 units. Workers per day are 1, 2, 3, ..., n. Work done in n days = 1 + 2 + 3 + ... + n n(n + 1)/2 = 276 23 × 24 ÷ 2 = 276 n = 23 days. Q43: Answer

Let initial number of workers = x. If no worker left, work would be completed in 12 days. Total work = 12x worker-days. Workers over 18 days form an AP: x, x − 6, x − 12, ..., x − 102. Total work done in 18 days = 18/2 × [2x − 17 × 6] = 9(2x − 102) So, 12x = 9(2x − 102) 12x = 18x − 918 6x = 918 x = 153 workers. Q44: Answer

Let the efficiency of one worker = 1 unit/day. One worker completes the work in 396 days, so total work = 396 units. Workers over n days are 5, 7, 9, ... This is an AP with first term 5 and common difference 2. Work done in n days = n/2 × [2 × 5 + (n − 1) × 2] = n/2 × [10 + 2n − 2] = n/2 × (2n + 8) = n(n + 4) n(n + 4) = 396 18 × 22 = 396 n = 18 days. Q45: Answer

Take total work = 72 units. A’s efficiency = 72 ÷ 24 = 3 units/day. B’s efficiency = 72 ÷ 36 = 2 units/day. C’s spoiling efficiency = 72 ÷ 72 = 1 unit/day. A and B together complete 3 + 2 = 5 units/day. Net work in one full 3-day cycle = 5 + 5 − 1 = 9 units. After 7 full cycles = 7 × 9 = 63 units completed. Remaining work = 72 − 63 = 9 units. Day 22: A and B complete 5 units. Remaining work = 9 − 5 = 4 units. Day 23: A and B can complete 5 units in 1 day. Time to complete remaining 4 units = 4/5 day. Total time = 21 + 1 + 4/5 = 22.8 days. 22.8 days is not given in options A–D. Therefore, answer is None of these. Q46: Answer

Given time is same for 18 men and 24 women. So, work done by 18 men = work done by 24 women. 18 men = 24 women. Efficiency ratio of one man to one woman = 24 : 18 = 4 : 3. A woman is less efficient by 4 − 3 = 1 unit on a base of 4 units. Required percentage = 1/4 × 100 = 25%. Q47: Answer
For the same work: 16 men × 18 days = 24 women × 16 days 288M = 384W M : W = 384 : 288 M : W = 4 : 3. Q48: Answer

Take total work = 72 units. Efficiency of one man = 72 ÷ 36 = 2 units/day. Efficiency of one woman = 72 ÷ 72 = 1 unit/day. Efficiency of 3 men and 6 women = 3 × 2 + 6 × 1 = 6 + 6 = 12 units/day. Time taken = 72 ÷ 12 = 6 days. Q49: Answer

Take total work = 80 units. Efficiency of one man = 80 ÷ 40 = 2 units/day. Efficiency of one woman = 80 ÷ 80 = 1 unit/day. Total efficiency of 6 men and 4 women = 6 × 2 + 4 × 1 = 12 + 4 = 16 units/day. Time taken = 80 ÷ 16 = 5 days. Q50: Answer

12 men can finish the job in 16 days. So, one man alone can complete the job in 12 × 16 = 192 days. 24 children can finish the job in 24 days. So, one child alone can complete the job in 24 × 24 = 576 days. Together time for 1 man and 1 child: = 192 × 576 ÷ (192 + 576) = 110592 ÷ 768 = 144 days.

questions.explanation: 12 men can finish the job in 16 days. So, one man alone can complete the job in 12 × 16 = 192 days. 24 children can finish the job in 24 days. So, one child alone can complete the job in 24 × 24 = 576 days. Together time for 1 man and 1 child: = 192 × 576 ÷ (192 + 576) = 110592 ÷ 768 = 144 days.

questions.text: Three bells ring at intervals of 14 minutes, 18 minutes and 30 minutes. If they ring together now, after how many minutes will they next ring together? तीन घंटिय ाँ 14 मिनि, 18 मिनि और 30 मिनि के अंतर ल पर बजती हैं। यटि वे अभी एक स थ बजती हैं, तो अगली ब र ककतने मिनि ब ि एक स थ बजेंगी? (A) 540 (B) 630 (C) 600 (D) 660 (E) 720
questions.prompt: Three bells ring at intervals of 14 minutes, 18 minutes and 30 minutes. questions.explanation: Required time = LCM(14, 18, 30) LCM = 2 × 32 × 5 × 7 = 630 Required answer = 630

questions.explanation: Product of the integers = HCF × LCM Other integer = 14 × 462/42 = 154 Required answer = 154

questions.text: The HCF and LCM of two positive integers are 18 and 720 respectively. If their sum is 234, find their positive difference. िो िन त्िक पूर् ांकों क िहत्ति सि पवतणक 18 और लघुत्ति सि पवत्यण 720 है। यटि उनक योग 234 है, तो उनक िन त्िक अंतर ज्ञ त कीजजए। (A) 54 (B) 36 (C) 45 (D) 63 (E) 72

questions.explanation: Let the integers be 18a and 18b, where HCF(a, b) = 1 ab = 720/18 = 40 and a + b = 234/18 = 13 The co-prime pair is 5 and 8 Difference = 18(8 - 5) = 54 Required answer = 54

questions.text: Pipe R can fill a storage tank in 51 hours and Pipe S can fill the same tank in 102 hours. If both pipes are opened together in an empty tank, how long will they take to fill it completely? पाइप R एक भंडारण टंकी को 51 घंटे में भर सकता है और पाइप S उसी टंकी को 102 घंटे में भर सकता है। यदि िोनों पाइपों को खाली टंकी में एक साथ खोल दिया जाए, तो उसे पूरी तरह भरने में ककतना समय लगेगा? questions.prompt: Pipe R can fill a storage tank in 51 hours and Pipe S can fill the same tank in 102 hours. How many more hours will the tank take to become full again? पाइप A और B क्रमशः 87 घंटे और 174 घंटे में टंकी भर सकते हैं। पाइप C भरी हुई टंकी को 145 घंटे में खाली कर सकता है। जब टंकी भरी हो, पाइप C को 25 घंटे के मलए खोला जाता है और किर बंि कर दिया जाता है। उसक े बाि खाली हुए भाग को भरने के मलए पाइप A और B साथ खोले जाते हैं। टंकी किर से पूरी भरने में और ककतने घंटे लगेंगे? (A) 10 hours (B) 12 hours (C) 15 hours (D) 18 hours (E) None of these
questions.prompt: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 87 hours and 174 hours, respectively. Pipe C can empty the full tank in 145 hours. When the tank is full, Pipe C is opened for 25 hours and then closed. After that, Pipes A and B are opened together to refill the emptied part. How many more hours will the tank take to become full again? पाइप A और B क्रमशः 87 घंटे और 174 घंटे में टंकी भर सकते हैं। पाइप C भरी हुई टंकी को 145 घंटे में खाली कर सकता है। जब टंकी भरी हो, पाइप C को 25 घंटे के मलए खोला जाता है और किर बंि कर दिया जाता है। उसक े बाि खाली हुए भाग को भरने के मलए पाइप A और B साथ खोले जाते हैं। टंकी किर से पूरी भरने में और ककतने घंटे लगेंगे?
questions.explanation: Take tank capacity = LCM of 87, 174 and 145 = 870 units. Pipe C’s emptying efficiency = 870 ÷ 145 = 6 units/hour. Work emptied by Pipe C in 25 hours = 6 × 25 = 150 units. Pipe A’s efficiency = 870 ÷ 87 = 10 units/hour. Pipe B’s efficiency = 870 ÷ 174 = 5 units/hour. Together filling efficiency = 10 + 5 = 15 units/hour. Time needed = 150 ÷ 15 = 10 hours.

questions.explanation: Take tank capacity = LCM of 40, 36 and 60 = 360 units. A’s efficiency = 360 ÷ 40 = 9 units/hour. B’s efficiency = 360 ÷ 36 = 10 units/hour. C’s emptying efficiency = 360 ÷ 60 = 6 units/hour. Work done in first 8 hours = (9 + 10 − 6) × 8 = 104 units. Remaining work = 360 − 104 = 256 units. After A is closed, net efficiency = 10 − 6 = 4 units/hour. Additional time = 256 ÷ 4 = 64 hours. Total time = 8 + 64 = 72 hours.

questions.prompt: Pipes P and Q can fill a tank in 54 hours and 72 hours, respectively. Pipe R is an outlet pipe. All three pipes are opened together in an empty tank. After 9 hours, Pipe P is closed. After another 15 hours, Pipe R is closed, and Pipe Q alone fills the remaining part in 52 more hours. In how many hours can Pipe R empty the full tank? पाइप P और Q क्रमशः 54 घंटे और 72 घंटे में टंकी भर सकते हैं। पाइप R एक आउटलेट पाइप है। तीनों पाइप खाली टंकी में एक साथ खोले जाते हैं। 9 घंटे बाि पाइप P बंि कर दिया जाता है। इसक े 15 घंटे बाि पाइप R बंि कर दिया जाता है, और पाइप Q अक े ला शेष भाग को 52 घंटे में भरता है। पाइप R भरी हुई टंकी को ककतने घंटे में खाली कर सकता है?
questions.explanation: Take tank capacity = LCM of 54 and 72 = 216 units. P’s efficiency = 216 ÷ 54 = 4 units/hour. Q’s efficiency = 216 ÷ 72 = 3 units/hour. Work filled by P = 4 × 9 = 36 units. Total working time of Q = 9 + 15 + 52 = 76 hours. Work filled by Q = 3 × 76 = 228 units. Total inlet work = 36 + 228 = 264 units. Extra work emptied by R = 264 − 216 = 48 units. R worked for 9 + 15 = 24 hours. R’s efficiency = 48 ÷ 24 = 2 units/hour. Time taken by R = 216 ÷ 2 = 108 hours.

questions.explanation: Take tank capacity = LCM of 70, 105 and 87 = 6090 units. A’s efficiency = 6090 ÷ 70 = 87 units/hour. B’s efficiency = 6090 ÷ 105 = 58 units/hour. Pipe C must empty 2030 units. Time for which C remains open = 2030 ÷ 70 = 29 hours.

questions.explanation: Pump fills per hour = 6 × 60 = 360 litres. Let tank capacity = C litres. Leak’s emptying rate = C ÷ 13 litres/hour. Net emptying rate = C ÷ 39 litres/hour. C/13 − 360 = C/39 3C − 14040 = C 2C = 14040 C = 7020 litres.

questions.explanation: Time to fill 2/5 tank with leak = 2/5 × 5d = 2d hours. Time to fill remaining 3/5 tank without leak = 3/5 × 25 = 15 hours. Total time = 31 hours. 2d + 15 = 31 2d = 16 d = 8.

questions.prompt: Pipe A is an inlet pipe, while Pipes B and C are outlet pipes. All three together can fill an empty tank in 80 hours. If Pipe C is closed after 10 hours, the tank gets filled 30 hours after Pipe C is closed. If Pipe B is closed after 10 hours instead, the tank gets filled 35 hours after Pipe B is closed. In how many hours can Pipe A alone fill the tank? पाइप A एक इनलेट पाइप है, जबकक पाइप B और C आउटलेट पाइप हैं। तीनों ममलकर खाली टंकी को 80 घंटे में भर सकते हैं। यदि 10 घंटे बाि पाइप C बंि कर दिया जाए, तो टंकी पाइप C बंि होने के 30 घंटे बाि भर जाती है। यदि इसक े बजाय 10 घंटे बाि पाइप B बंि कर दिया जाए, तो टंकी पाइप B बंि होने के 35 घंटे बाि भर जाती है। पाइप A अक े ला टंकी को ककतने घंटे में भर सकता है?
questions.explanation: Take tank capacity = 240 units. Efficiency of A + B + C together = 240 ÷ 80 = 3 units/hour. Work done in first 10 hours = 3 × 10 = 30 units. Remaining work = 240 − 30 = 210 units. When C is closed, A + B net efficiency = 210 ÷ 30 = 7 units/hour. When B is closed, A + C net efficiency = 210 ÷ 35 = 6 units/hour. A + B + C net efficiency = 3 units/hour. A’s efficiency = 7 + 6 − 3 = 10 units/hour. Time taken by A = 240 ÷ 10 = 24 hours.

questions.explanation: Efficiency ratio A : C = 2 : 3. Let A’s efficiency = 6 units/minute and C’s efficiency = 9 units/minute. A + B and B + C efficiencies are in the ratio 55 : 70 = 11 : 14. So, A + B = 11 units/minute and B + C = 14 units/minute. B’s efficiency = 11 − 6 = 5 units/minute. Tank capacity = 70 × 11 = 770 units. Time taken by B = 770 ÷ 5 = 154 minutes.

If the filling rate of Pipe B is 3/2 of the emptying rate of Pipe C, in how many hours can Pipe A alone fill the tank? पाइप A और B इनलेट पाइप हैं, और पाइप C एक आउटलेट पाइप है। खाली टंकी से शुरू करते हुए, पाइप A और C को 37 घंटे के मलए साथ खोला जाता है। इसक े बाि पाइप B और C शेष भाग को 74 घंटे में भरते हैं। यदि पाइप B की भरने की िर, पाइप C की खाली करने की िर की 3/2 है, तो पाइप A अक े ला टंकी को ककतने घंटे में भर सकता है?
questions.explanation: Let Pipe C’s emptying efficiency = 2 units/hour. Then Pipe B’s filling efficiency = 3 units/hour. Pipe C remains open for 37 + 74 = 111 hours. Work emptied by C = 2 × 111 = 222 units. Work filled by B in 74 hours = 3 × 74 = 222 units. So, B’s filling exactly cancels C’s emptying. Therefore, Pipe A fills the whole tank in 37 hours.

questions.explanation: Extra time due to leak in first case = 66 − 48 = 18 hours. Extra time due to leak in second case = 57 − 48 = 9 hours. So, leak-open times are in the ratio 18 : 9 = 2 : 1. 66 − y = 2 × [57 − (y + 5)] 66 − y = 2 × (52 − y) 66 − y = 104 − 2y y = 38.

questions.explanation: New time of A = 75 ÷ 125% = 60 hours. New time of B = 72 ÷ 80% = 90 hours. Take tank capacity = LCM of 60 and 90 = 180 units. A’s new efficiency = 180 ÷ 60 = 3 units/hour. questions.prompt: Pipe A can fill a tank in 30 minutes, while Pipe B can empty the full tank in 60 minutes. questions.explanation: At 75% efficiency, Pipe A fills the tank in 30 ÷ 75% = 40 minutes. At 50% efficiency, Pipe B empties the tank in 60 ÷ 50% = 120 minutes. questions.prompt: Two inlet pipes A and B can fill a tank in 30 minutes and 40 minutes, respectively. Because of blockage, A works at half of its normal rate and B works at two-thirds of its normal rate. questions.explanation: Take tank capacity = LCM of 30 and 40 = 120 units. A’s normal efficiency = 120 ÷ 30 = 4 units/minute. B’s normal efficiency = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 units/minute. Blocked efficiency = 4 × 1/2 + 3 × 2/3 = 2 + 2 = 4 units/minute. Work done at full capacity in 8 minutes = (4 + 3) × 8 = 56 units. Remaining work done during blockage = 120 − 56 = 64 units. Blocked time = 64 ÷ 4 = 16 minutes.

questions.explanation: Let the efficiencies of P and Q be p and q. 17p + 22q = 1 16 × 50% × p + 28q = 1 8p + 28q = 1 So, 17p + 22q = 8p + 28q 9p = 6q p : q = 2 : 3. Tank capacity = 17 × 2 + 22 × 3 = 100 units. Together efficiency = 2 + 3 = 5 units/hour. Time taken = 100 ÷ 5 = 20 hours.

questions.prompt: Pipe P, working at 80% of its full efficiency, can fill a tank in 70 hours. In how many hours can Pipes P and Q together fill the whole tank? पाइप P, Q और R इनलेट पाइप हैं। यदि पाइप P को खाली टंकी में 18 घंटे के मलए खोला जाए, तो पाइप Q शेष भाग को 54 घंटे में भर सकता है। यदि पाइप R टंकी के 2/5 भाग को भरता है, तो पाइप Q शेष भाग को 36 घंटे में भर सकता है। पाइप P और Q ममलकर पूरी टंकी को ककतने घंटे में भर सकते हैं?
questions.explanation: Pipe Q fills 3/5 of the tank in 36 hours. Time taken by Q to fill the whole tank = 36 ÷ 3/5 = 60 hours. In the first case, Q fills 54 ÷ 60 = 9/10 of the tank. So, P fills 1/10 of the tank in 18 hours. Time taken by P to fill the whole tank = 18 × 10 = 180 hours. Together time of P and Q = (180 × 60) ÷ (180 + 60) = 45 hours.

questions.explanation: Let the efficiencies of A, B and C be A, B and C. Together efficiency = A + B + C. When C is closed 5 hours before x and the tank is filled in x + 1 hours: (A + B + C)(x − 5) + (A + B) × 6 = (A + B + C)x 6(A + B) = 5(A + B + C) A + B = 5C. When B is closed 8 hours before x and the tank is filled in x + 2 hours: (A + B + C)(x − 8) + (A + C) × 10 = (A + B + C)x 10(A + C) = 8(A + B + C) A + C = 4B. From A + B = 5C and A + C = 4B: A : B : C = 19 : 6 : 5. Time ratio of A and B = 1/19 : 1/6 = 6 : 19. Difference in times = 19 − 6 = 13 parts. 13 parts = 78 hours. A’s time = 6 parts = 78 × 6 ÷ 13 = 36 hours.
